title: Arteriogram with Possible Embolization
summary: Arteriography with possible embolization for arterial hemorrhage, including trauma and GI bleeding.
provenance: Imported from procedure orders PDF updated 4.15.26

items: Traumatic arterial bleeding with instability or ongoing transfusion needs.
Persistent/recurrent GI bleeding after failed or infeasible endoscopy.
Active arterial bleeding or symptomatic pseudoaneurysm.
No safe arterial access or catheter route (relative).
Uncorrectable coagulopathy or severe contrast reaction requires individualized planning; weigh against hemorrhage urgency.
No safe embolization target or unacceptable risk to essential organ/bowel perfusion.
A source requiring immediate surgery or another treatment: coordinate the appropriate pathway.
High bleeding risk.
Anticoagulation should already be held for active bleeding; confirm last doses and any reversal given.
Warfarin: hold 5 days and confirm INR <= 1.8.
IV unfractionated heparin: hold 4-6 hours and check aPTT or anti-Xa level.
Enoxaparin: hold 1 dose if prophylactic; hold 2 doses or 24 hours if therapeutic.
DOAC timing is agent-, dose-, and renal-function-specific; use the anticoagulation table.
Clopidogrel and ticagrelor: hold 5 days; prasugrel: hold 7 days.
Aspirin: hold 3-5 days.
Active major hemorrhage: review last doses and reversal with the treating team; elective hold intervals must not delay life-saving source control.
Platelets >50,000/µL.
NPO (if moderate sedation).
Vital signs per routine.
PIV placement (not left arm).
Glucose POC.
Most recent CBC, INR, and CMP.

Arteriogram with Possible Embolization
Bleeding.
Infection.
Damage to nearby structures.
Vessel injury, including dissection or rupture.
Nontarget embolization and organ/tissue ischemia; bowel ischemia in GI cases.
Persistent or recurrent bleeding requiring repeat embolization or surgery.
left gastric, splenic, and common hepatic branches supply the foregut. The gastroduodenal artery (GDA) usually arises from the common hepatic artery.
inferior pancreaticoduodenal, jejunal/ileal, ileocolic, right colic (variable), and middle colic branches supply distal duodenum through proximal two-thirds of transverse colon.
left colic, sigmoid, and superior rectal branches supply distal transverse/descending colon, sigmoid, and upper rectum.
pancreaticoduodenal arcades connect celiac and SMA territories; marginal colonic arteries connect SMA and IMA. Prior surgery can alter these routes.
map replaced/accessory hepatic arteries. Trauma targets may involve splenic, renal, pelvic/internal iliac, or chest-wall branches rather than GI vessels.
femoral puncture should permit compression over the femoral head; radial access requires an appropriate artery and a patent route to the target.
localize bleeding and review variants/collaterals.
use ultrasound-guided femoral or radial access; place the sheath.
perform angiography to identify extravasation or pseudoaneurysm.
advance the microcatheter; confirm the target and branches to preserve.
coils, gelatin, particles, or liquid agent according to target and flow.
watch for reflux, catheter movement, and nontarget filling.
confirm hemostasis, assess collateral filling, and preserve uninvolved perfusion.
obtain access hemostasis and document the treatment and handoff.
bleeding may be intermittent or obscured by vasospasm; correlate CTA/endoscopy and discuss a targeted plan rather than indiscriminate embolization.
recheck the tip before delivery; stop injection if reflux or nontarget filling appears.
keep treatment selective, preserve collaterals, and account for prior surgery, radiation, or poor baseline perfusion.
collaterals can refill the lesion; assess relevant inflow/outflow, especially GDA/pancreaticoduodenal pathways.
avoid forceful wire advancement, wedged injections, and unnecessary manipulation; reassess new dissection or extravasation.
check access-site swelling and distal perfusion; persistent instability needs prompt reassessment even after an angiographic endpoint.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
Monitor color of access site.
Vital signs every 15 minutes x 4, then every 30 minutes x 2, then every 1 hour x 4, then every 4 hours; edit to match bedrest.

blocks.title: Access care
items: Bedrest 2 hours with closure device; 6 hours with manual compression.

1: Remove radial artery compression device within 2 hours post procedure.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: 24 hours.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours.
DOACs: Typically 24 hours; confirm agent and renal function.
Clopidogrel: 75 mg dose - 6 hours; 300-600 mg loading dose - 24 hours.
Aspirin: 24 hours.
Restart after hemostasis is confirmed; individualize timing for procedure-specific or patient-specific exceptions.

blocks.title: Discharge
items: Discharge order with medication reconciliation - 2-6 hours.
After visit summary: .IRAVSARTERIOGRAM.
